preamble.summary: Psalm 103 (MT) / Psalm 102 (LXX) is the Psalter's greatest CHESED-hymn — a Davidic meditation structured by the 'Bless the LORD, O my soul' inclusio (vv. 1, 22). It cites Exodus 34:6 ('the LORD, merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love,' v. 8) and develops the forgive-as-the-east-is-from-the-west chesed theology (v. 12). Henry Francis Lyte's 1834 hymn 'Praise, My Soul, the King of Heaven' is a beloved paraphrase.
preamble.notable_variants: 103:8 Exodus 34:6 citation as divine-character-revelation; 103:12 'as far as the east is from the west' as forgive-distance theology; 103:13 'as a father has compassion on his children' → fatherhood-of-God theology; 103:20–21 angelic-hosts-blessing-the-LORD.
preamble.structural_notes: MT Ps 103 = LXX Ps 102. 22 verses. Great chesed-hymn.

variant_notes: 'Of David. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name!' tracks MT. The INCLUSIO formula — 'Bless the LORD, O my soul' opens (v. 1) and closes (v. 22). Self-addressing-soul pattern.
'Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits' tracks MT. FORGET-NOT-BENEFITS — the anti-amnesia-of-grace pastoral.

'Who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases' tracks MT. FORGIVES + HEALS — paired divine-actions. Jesus' 'which is easier, to say your sins are forgiven or to say rise and walk?' (Matt 9:5) presupposes this paired-theology.
'Who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy' tracks MT. CROWN-OF-CHESED-AND-MERCY. The 'crown' image for divine-benefaction.
'Who satisfies you with good so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's' tracks MT. EAGLE-YOUTH-RENEWAL. Isaiah 40:31 ('they shall mount up with wings like eagles') parallels.
'The LORD works righteousness and justice for all who are oppressed' tracks MT.
'He made known his ways to Moses, his acts to the people of Israel' tracks MT. MOSES-AS-RECIPIENT-OF-DIVINE-WAYS theology.

'The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love' tracks MT. EXODUS 34:6 CITATION. The most-cited OT divine-character formula — also cited at Num 14:18, Neh 9:17, Ps 86:15, 145:8, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2, Nahum 1:3. The definitive divine-self-revelation.
'He will not always chide, nor will he keep his anger forever' tracks MT.

'He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities' tracks MT. NOT-DEAL-ACCORDING-TO-SINS theology — the grace-principle. Ezra 9:13 ('you our God have punished us less than our iniquities deserved') parallels.
'For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him' tracks MT. HEAVENS-HIGH-OVER-EARTH chesed-scale.

'As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us' tracks MT. EAST-FROM-WEST FORGIVENESS. The infinite-horizontal-distance (unlike north-south which meets at the poles) — transgressions removed INDEFINITELY. The image is one of the Psalter's most-quoted forgive-vocabulary.

'As a father shows compassion to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him' tracks MT. FATHER-COMPASSION-ANALOGY. Luke 15's Prodigal-Son parable (the father who runs-to-embrace) and the Abba-Father of Mark 14:36, Rom 8:15, Gal 4:6 fulfill the fatherhood-of-God theology this verse grounds.

'For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust' tracks MT. DUST-REMEMBRANCE — divine-awareness of human-frailty. Genesis 2:7's 'formed the man of dust' and 3:19's 'to dust you shall return' background.
'As for man, his days are like grass; he flourishes like a flower of the field' tracks MT. GRASS-AND-FLOWER transience. Isaiah 40:6–8 develops; 1 Peter 1:24 cites.
'For the wind passes over it, and it is gone, and its place knows it no more' tracks MT.
'But the steadfast love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness to children's children' tracks MT.
'To those who keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments' tracks MT.
'The LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all' tracks MT.
'Bless the LORD, O you his angels, you mighty ones who do his word, obeying the voice of his word!' tracks MT. ANGELS-BLESS-THE-LORD. The angelic-worship-call.
'Bless the LORD, all his hosts, his ministers, who do his will!' tracks MT. HOSTS / MINISTERS. Hebrews 1:14 ('ministering spirits,' leitourgika pneumata) draws on this minister-angel vocabulary.

'Bless the LORD, all his works, in all places of his dominion. Bless the LORD, O my soul!' tracks MT. FOUR-FOLD 'BLESS THE LORD' closing (vv. 20–22) — angels, hosts, all-works, own-soul. The inclusio returns: 'Bless the LORD, O my soul' frames the whole psalm.
